title: Tenant Isolation SLI Derivation and Dashboard Primer
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable primer for deriving tenant-level SLIs and building compact operator dashboards. Focus: hosted + dedicated multi-tenant inference paths where tenant isolation and noisy-neighbor effects are primary concerns. This is a working doc — aim is to land a minimal dashboard surface and SLI derivation that other teams can iterate on.

Scope and assumptions:
- We assume request metadata contains tenant_id, plan_tier (free/standard/premium), region, model_name, model_variant, request_size_tokens, and trace_id.
- Metric collection can be done either at ingress proxy (frontdoor) or at runtime nodes; prefer ingress-derived high-level SLIs and runtime-derived low-level signals for root cause.
- Billing/cost metrics are out-of-scope for SLOs but must be surfaced alongside SLIs.

Principles for tenant SLIs (short):
1) Keep SLIs composable: derive per-request booleans (success, bounded_latency, cache_hit) and aggregate.
2) Prefilter by stable identifiers: tenant_id + plan_tier. Avoid including volatile labels (ephemeral session ids) as aggregation keys.
3) Monitor both user-facing and runtime-facing signals: p50/p95 user-latency vs runtime tail CPU/GPU contention.
4) Make dashboards cheap: pre-aggregate 1m/5m and use rollup tables for high-cardinality views.

Core SLI candidates (definitions):
- tenant_request_success_rate: (# requests with http_code in 2xx and model returned tokens > 0) / total requests. Use ingress tags. Window: 5m sliding.
- tenant_inference_latency_p95_ms: 95th percentile of total end-to-end time (ingress->response). Unit: ms. Window: 5m rolling; compute both p50/p95/p99.
- tenant_runtime_queue_time_p95_ms: p95 of time spent queued on runtime node before kernel execution. Derived from runtime span: queue.start -> kernel.start.
- tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate: tokens served from prefix/KV cache / total tokens served for requests with cache-eligible model variants. Important: sample only requests with request_size_tokens >= X to avoid noise from micro-requests.
- tenant_batching_efficiency: average tokens-per-batch / configured_target_tokens_per_batch. Range: 0..inf. Low values indicate poor batching and higher cost.
- tenant_tail_throttle_rate: fraction of requests that got throttled or rate-limited at ingress or runtime. Includes 429/503 responses.
- tenant_model_fallback_rate: fraction of requests routed to fallback model variant (e.g., quantized or smaller) due to capacity.
- tenant_error_class_rate: map of error classes (model-crash, oom, timeout, invalid-input) -> fraction.

Why these: they cover correctness, latency, cost-levers (cache/batching), and operational degradation patterns.

Tracing and span design (practical guide):
- Start traces at ingress with span name: ingress.request.start and tags: tenant_id, plan_tier, model_name, request_size_tokens, region. Ensure trace_id is propagated downstream.
- Runtime spans: runtime.receive, runtime.schedule.queue, runtime.kernel.start, runtime.kernel.end, runtime.emit.response. Attach runtime.instance_id, gpu_id, sv_mem_util_pct.
- Client-visible latency = time(ingress.request.start -> ingress.response.end). Runtime latency = runtime.kernel.start -> runtime.kernel.end + queue time.
- Low-cardinality tagging: include tenant_tier and model_shard but avoid per-tenant feature flags as tags. If need per-tenant debug, use ephemeral debug flag that creates a separate high-sampling path.
- Sampling policy: default 0.5% global sample for full traces; dynamic bump to 100% for tenants with SLO burn > 10% in last 30m (see runbook action). If debug mode enabled (ticket ID), capture 100% for that tenant for up to 1 hour.

Dashboard design recommendations (operator-first):
Minimal operator page (single pane for fast triage)
- Top row: global SLO summary for selected tenant (percent success, p95 latency, error budget burn). Small sparkline for 6h.
- Left column: latency slices by component (ingress, queue, kernel execution) with p50/p95/p99 and recent top traces link.
- Middle column: cost and efficiency levers: kv_cache_hit_rate, batching_efficiency, avg_tokens_per_request, request_rate.
- Right column: failure taxonomy (error_class_rate pie), model_fallback_rate, throttle_rate.
- Drilldowns: time-series with tenant selector + compare-to-baseline button (baseline = median of same-tier tenants over last 7d).
- Action controls: quick-set to raise trace sampling to 100% for tenant, toggle debug logging link (opens permissioned runbook), increment routing fallback to smaller model.

Query budgeting & widget hygiene:
- Avoid high-cardinality live queries in top-level dashboard. Use precomputed rollups for tenant-level metrics at 1m buckets.
- Heavy investigations should use a dedicated investigation dashboard with raw traces and a request-level table (limit 1000 rows).
- Include a cost estimate badge per panel (approx. query cost / month) so dashboard owners are aware.

Alerting guidance (lightweight):
- Per-tenant burn alert: if error_budget_used_percent >= 25% in last 30m AND error_budget_used_percent >= 10% absolute then page SRE rotation. (This is a conservative starting threshold.)
- Latency spike rapid alert: tenant_inference_latency_p95_ms increases by > 2x over 15m relative to last 24h median -> page oncall.
- Slow-degradation alert (warning): kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 15% relative to 3h baseline -> create ticket to investigate cache eviction patterns.

Runbook snippet for high SLO burn (triage checklist):
1) Look at top-level dashboard for tenant and confirm which SLI is burning (errors vs latency vs throttle).
2) If error-type dominated: open traces filtered by tenant_id + error_class and inspect recent spans. Check for common runtime.instance_id or gpu_id.
3) If latency or tail latency: inspect runtime_queue_time and kernel execution time breakdown. If queue_time high, suspect capacity pressure -> check instance pool utilization, autoscaler events, and scheduling logs.
4) If kv_cache_hit_rate low: check cache evictions on shard (cache metrics), model variant policy changes, or recent rollout.
5) If model_fallback_rate high: verify routing config, check for model-serving OOMs or pod restarts in last 30m. Consider temporary routing override to a larger pool.
6) If unknown: bump trace sampling to 100% for tenant for 20 min, enable debug logs (use ticket gating), and collect 200 sample traces for postmortem.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to calculate tenant-level token-weighted SLI when tenants have widely different request sizes? Proposal: weight latency SLI by tokens-per-request (configurable). Need a small experiment to validate signal stability — ticket INF-3011.
- We need a canonical datastore for tenant->billing_tier mapping to avoid inconsistencies between ingress and billing reports. Action: infra + billing sync.
- Decide retention policy for tenant-level traces when debug sampling is triggered — currently may blow storage. Proposal: auto-prune traces older than 7d for debug bursts.

Implementation notes / pragmatics:
- Metric schema: prefer metrics with tags [tenant_id, plan_tier, region, model_name, model_variant]. For low-cardinality operator view, drop tenant_id to show aggregated tier views.
- Use pre-aggregated summaries exported to metrics-store every 1m to avoid expensive live joins from raw request logs.
- Add a "tenant_tagging" middleware at ingress to validate tenant_id and enrich requests with plan_tier and billing_id. Fail-open to allow request processing to continue even if enrichment fails — but log as metric.

Examples (alert rules pseudo):
- name: tenant_latency_p95_spike
  expr: (tenant_inference_latency_p95_ms{tenant_id="TEAMX"} > 2 * baseline_24h_median(tenant_inference_latency_p95_ms{tenant_id="TEAMX"}))
  for: 15m
  actions: page_oncall

- name: tenant_cache_eviction_warning
  expr: (tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate{plan_tier="standard"} < (avg_over_time(tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate{plan_tier="standard"}[3h]) - 0.15))
  for: 10m
  actions: create_ticket(team=serving-runtime)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — aim for immediate value (reduce noise from high-card dashboards) rather than exhaustive metric coverage.
- If you own a tenant-facing product page that needs different slices (e.g., real-time chat vs batch embedding lanes), call that out and we will parameterize the tenant selector.

References and related pages:
- infra/kv-cache-sharding-design (link internal)
- confluence:Observability-MultiTenant-Guide (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira: INF-2142 (tracing sampling policy)

Sign-off checklist before shipping to Console team:
- [ ] agree on canonical tenant->tier source
- [ ] build 1m pre-aggregation pipeline for tenant-level metrics
- [ ] implement sampling toggle API for ops (RBAC guarded)
- [ ] produce a single-page operator dashboard prototype and run pilot with 3 tenants

Unpolished notes / scratch ideas (leave in doc):
- Could present a compact health vector per tenant: H = [success_rate, p95_latency_norm, cache_eff, fallback_rate] colored band. Easy to scan.
- Consider tenant anomaly detection baseline based on same-tier cohort median + MAD to reduce false positives from seasonal tenants.

Author: Maya Singh (eng-observability). Last edits include sample thresholds and runbook actions.
